summary: On Erev Pesach, we do not eat close to the evening, so we can eat matzah with an appetite. At the Seder, even the poorest person leans and gets four cups of wine.

chunks.en: On Erev Pesach, close to Mincha time,
chunks.st: On the eve of Passover, adjacent to minḥa time,

chunks.en: a person should not eat until it gets dark.
chunks.explain: So he will eat the matzah at night with an appetite.
chunks.st: a person may not eat until dark,
chunks.stMore: so that he will be able to eat matza that night with a hearty appetite.

chunks.en: And even the poorest person in Israel should
chunks.st: Even the poorest of Jews should

chunks.en: not eat until he leans.
chunks.explain: He leans to the left, like free and rich people.
chunks.st: not eat the meal on Passover night until he reclines on his left side,
chunks.stMore: as free and wealthy people recline when they eat.

chunks.en: And they should not give him less than four
chunks.st: And the distributors of charity should not give a poor person less than four

chunks.en: cups of wine,
chunks.st: cups of wine for the Festival meal of Passover night.

chunks.en: even if he gets his food from the charity plate.
chunks.st: And this halakha applies even if the poor person is one of the poorest members of society and receives his food from the charity plate.

words.note: Food given to the poorest people.

summary: At the Seder, Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue which bracha comes first over the first cup: the bracha on the day (Kiddush) or the bracha on the wine.
stIntro: The tanna describes the beginning of the Passover seder.

chunks.en: They poured for him the first cup.
chunks.st: The attendants poured the wine of the first cup for the leader of the seder.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he says the bracha on the day,
chunks.st: One recites the blessing over the sanctification of the day, i.e., the kiddush for the Festival: Who blesses Israel and the Festivals,

chunks.en: and after that he says the bracha on the wine.
chunks.st: and thereafter he recites the blessing over the wine: Who creates fruit of the vine.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he says the bracha on the wine,
chunks.st: One recites the blessing over the wine

chunks.en: and after that he says the bracha on the day.
chunks.st: and thereafter recites the blessing over the day.

summary: This mishnah describes the foods brought to the Seder table: vegetables, matzah, maror, charoses, two cooked foods, and in the time of the Beis Hamikdash, the korban Pesach.

chunks.en: They brought food in front of him.
chunks.st: The attendants brought vegetables before the leader of the seder prior to the meal,
chunks.stMore: if there were no other vegetables on the table.

chunks.en: He dips the lettuce
chunks.st: He dips the ḥazeret into water or vinegar, to taste some food

chunks.en: before he gets to the maror that goes with the bread.
chunks.explain: Maror, which is eaten after the matzah.
chunks.st: before he reaches the dessert of the bread, i.e., the bitter herbs, which were eaten after the matza.

chunks.en: They brought in front of him matzah, lettuce,
chunks.st: They brought before him matza and ḥazeret

chunks.en: charoses, and two cooked foods,
chunks.st: and ḥaroset, and at least two cooked dishes in honor of the Festival.

words.note: A sweet dip for the maror.

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין חֲרֹסֶת מִצְוָה.
chunks.en: even though charoses is not a mitzvah.
chunks.st: The tanna comments that this was the practice, although eating ḥaroset is not a mitzva but merely a custom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Tzadok says:

chunks.en: it is a mitzvah. And in the Beis Hamikdash they would bring in front of him
chunks.st: Actually, it is a mitzva to eat ḥaroset. And in the period when the Temple stood and they offered the Paschal lamb, they brought before him

chunks.en: the korban Pesach itself.
chunks.st: the body of the Paschal lamb.

summary: When the second cup is poured, the son asks Mah Nishtanah, and the father teaches him the story of leaving Mitzrayim.

chunks.en: They poured for him the second cup,
chunks.st: The attendants poured the second cup for the leader of the seder,

chunks.en: and here the son asks his father.
chunks.st: and here the son asks his father the questions about the differences between Passover night and a regular night.

chunks.en: And if the son does not understand enough,
chunks.st: And if the son does not have the intelligence to ask questions on his own,

chunks.en: his father teaches him:
chunks.st: his father teaches him the questions.

chunks.he: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה מִכָּל הַלֵּילוֹת,
chunks.en: Why is this night different from all other nights?
chunks.st: Why is this night different from all other nights?

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין חָמֵץ וּמַצָּה,
chunks.en: On all other nights we eat chametz and matzah,
chunks.st: As on all other nights we eat leavened bread and matza as preferred;

chunks.en: this night only matzah.
chunks.st: on this night all our bread is matza.

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין שְׁאָר יְרָקוֹת,
chunks.en: On all other nights we eat all kinds of vegetables,
chunks.st: As on all other nights we eat other vegetables;

chunks.en: this night maror.
chunks.st: on this night we eat bitter herbs.
chunks.stMore: The mishna continues its list of the questions.

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין בָּשָׂר צָלִי,
chunks.en: On all other nights we eat meat roasted,
chunks.st: When the Temple was standing one would ask: As on all other nights we eat either roasted,

chunks.en: boiled, or cooked,
chunks.st: stewed, or cooked meat,

chunks.en: this night only roasted.
chunks.explain: The korban Pesach, in the time of the Beis Hamikdash.
chunks.st: but on this night all the meat is the roasted meat of the Paschal lamb.

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ מַטְבִּילִין פַּעַם אַחַת,
chunks.en: On all other nights we dip one time,
chunks.st: The final question was asked even after the destruction of the Temple: As on all other nights we dip the vegetables in a liquid during the meal only once;

chunks.en: this night two times.
chunks.st: however, on this night we dip twice.

chunks.en: And according to how much the son understands,
chunks.st: And according to the intelligence and the ability of the son,

chunks.en: his father teaches him.
chunks.st: his father teaches him about the Exodus.
chunks.stMore: When teaching his son about the Exodus.

chunks.en: He begins with the shame and ends with the praise,
chunks.explain: How bad it was for us, and how Hashem saved us.
chunks.st: He begins with the Jewish people’s disgrace and concludes with their glory.

chunks.en: and he explains from "An Arami tried to destroy my father,"
chunks.st: And he expounds from the passage: “An Aramean tried to destroy my father” (Deuteronomy 26:5), the declaration one recites when presenting his first fruits at the Temple,

chunks.en: until he finishes the whole parshah.
chunks.st: until he concludes explaining the entire section.

summary: Rabban Gamliel teaches that at the Seder we must explain Pesach, matzah and maror. Every person must see himself as if he left Mitzrayim, so we thank and praise Hashem.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel used to say,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel would say:

chunks.en: anyone who did not say three
chunks.st: Anyone who did not say

chunks.en: of these things on Pesach
chunks.st: these three matters on Passover

chunks.en: did not do his mitzvah.
chunks.st: has not fulfilled his obligation:

chunks.en: And they are:
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: Pesach, matzah,
chunks.st: matza,

chunks.en: and maror. Pesach,
chunks.st: and bitter herbs. When one mentions these matters, he must elaborate and explain them: The Paschal lamb is brought

chunks.en: because Hashem passed over
chunks.st: because the Omnipresent passed over [pasaḥ]

chunks.en: the houses of our fathers in Mitzrayim.
chunks.st: the houses of our forefathers in Egypt,
chunks.stMore: as it is stated: “That you shall say: It is the sacrifice of the Lord’s Paschal offering for He passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses” (Exodus 12:27).

chunks.he: מַצָּה, עַל שׁוּם שֶׁנִּגְאֲלוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרַיִם.
chunks.en: Matzah, because our fathers were redeemed in Mitzrayim.
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel continues to explain: The reason for matza is because our forefathers were redeemed from Egypt,
chunks.stMore: as it is stated: “And they baked the dough that they took out of Egypt as cakes of matzot, for it was not leavened, as they were thrust out of Egypt and could not tarry, neither had they prepared for themselves any victual” (Exodus 12:39).

chunks.en: Maror, because the Mitzrim made bitter
chunks.st: The reason for bitter herbs is because the Egyptians embittered

chunks.en: the lives of our fathers in Mitzrayim.
chunks.st: our forefathers’ lives in Egypt,
chunks.stMore: as it is stated: “And they embittered their lives with hard service, in mortar and in brick; in all manner of service in the field, all the service that they made them serve was with rigor” (Exodus 1:14).

chunks.he: בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר חַיָּב אָדָם לִרְאוֹת
chunks.en: In every generation, a person must see
chunks.st: The tanna of the mishna further states: In each and every generation a person must view

chunks.he: אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְאִלּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם,
chunks.en: himself as if he left Mitzrayim,
chunks.st: himself as though he personally left Egypt,

chunks.en: as it says (Shemos 13),
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: "And you shall tell your son on that day, saying,
chunks.st: And you shall tell your son on that day, saying:

chunks.en: 'Because of this, Hashem did
chunks.st: It is because of this which the Lord did

chunks.en: for me when I left Mitzrayim.'"
chunks.st: for me when I came forth out of Egypt” (Exodus 13:8).
chunks.stMore: In every generation, each person must say: “This which the Lord did for me,” and not: This which the Lord did for my forefathers.

chunks.en: So we must thank,
chunks.st: The mishna continues with the text of the Haggadah. Therefore we are obligated to thank,

chunks.en: praise, glorify,
chunks.st: praise, glorify,

chunks.en: honor, raise up,
chunks.st: extol, exalt,

chunks.en: give glory, bless,
chunks.st: honor, bless,

chunks.en: lift up, and praise
chunks.st: revere, and laud [lekales]

chunks.en: the One who did for our fathers and for us
chunks.st: the One who performed for our forefathers and for us

chunks.en: all these miracles.
chunks.st: all these miracles:

chunks.en: He took us out from slavery to freedom,
chunks.st: He took us out from slavery to freedom,

chunks.en: from sadness to joy,
chunks.st: from sorrow to joy,

chunks.en: and from mourning to Yom Tov,
chunks.st: from mourning to a Festival,

chunks.en: and from darkness to great light,
chunks.st: from darkness to a great light,

chunks.en: and from being slaves to being redeemed.
chunks.st: and from enslavement to redemption.

chunks.en: And let us say before Him, Halleluyah!
chunks.st: And we will say before Him: Halleluya.
chunks.stMore: At this point one recites the hallel that is said on all joyous days. Since one does not complete hallel at this point in the seder, the mishna asks:

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue how much of Hallel is said before the meal. Then Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva teach how the bracha of redemption ends.

chunks.en: How far does he say?
chunks.explain: How much of Hallel before the meal.
chunks.st: Until where does one recite hallel?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: until "a happy mother of children."
chunks.st: Until “Who makes the barren woman dwell in her house as a joyful mother of children, halleluya” (Psalms 113:9).

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: until "the flint into a spring of water."
chunks.st: Until “Who turned the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a fountain of waters” (Psalms 114:8).

chunks.en: And he ends with a bracha of redemption.
chunks.st: And one concludes this section of hallel with a blessing that refers to redemption.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says that although one should recite:

chunks.he: אֲשֶׁר גְּאָלָנוּ וְגָאַל אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם,
chunks.en: "Who redeemed us and redeemed our fathers from Mitzrayim,"
chunks.st: Who redeemed us and redeemed our forefathers from Egypt,

chunks.en: and he did not end with "Baruch Atah."
chunks.st: one who did so would not conclude with the formula: Blessed are You, Lord.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says that one recites a different version of this blessing:

chunks.he: כֵּן ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ יַגִּיעֵנוּ
chunks.en: "So may Hashem our God and the God of our fathers bring us
chunks.st: So too, the Lord our God and the God of our forefathers will bring us

chunks.he: לְמוֹעֲדִים וְלִרְגָלִים אֲחֵרִים הַבָּאִים לִקְרָאתֵנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם,
chunks.en: to other holidays and Yamim Tovim that come toward us in peace,
chunks.st: to future holidays and Festivals in peace,

chunks.en: happy in the building of Your city and joyful in Your service.
chunks.st: happy over the building of Your city and joyous in Your service.

chunks.en: And we will eat there from the korbanos
chunks.st: And there we will eat from the Paschal lamb

chunks.en: and from the korbanos Pesach," and so on,
chunks.st: and other offerings, etc.,

chunks.he: עַד בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה' גָּאַל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
chunks.en: until "Baruch Atah Hashem, who redeemed Israel."
chunks.st: until: Blessed are You, Lord, Who redeemed Israel.

summary: This mishnah teaches what we say over the third and fourth cups, and when we may drink more wine.

chunks.en: They poured for him the third cup,
chunks.st: They poured for the leader of the seder the third cup of wine,

chunks.en: he says the bracha on his food.
chunks.st: and he recites the blessing over his food, Grace After Meals.

chunks.en: The fourth: he finishes Hallel over it,
chunks.st: Next, they pour him the fourth cup. He completes hallel over it, as he already recited the first part of hallel before the meal.

chunks.en: and he says over it the bracha of song.
chunks.st: And he also recites the blessing of the song at the end of hallel over the fourth cup.

chunks.en: Between these cups,
chunks.st: During the period between these cups, i.e., the first three cups established by the Sages,

chunks.en: if he wants to drink,
chunks.st: if one wishes to drink more

chunks.en: he may drink. Between the third and the fourth,
chunks.st: he may drink; however, between the third cup and the fourth cup one should

chunks.en: he should not drink.
chunks.st: not drink.

summary: This mishnah teaches not to eat anything after the korban Pesach, and what happens if people fell asleep during the meal.

chunks.en: And we do not end after the korban Pesach with afikoman.
chunks.explain: We do not eat dessert or snacks after it.
chunks.st: One does not conclude after the Paschal lamb with an afikoman.

chunks.en: If some of them fell asleep,
chunks.st: If some of the participants at the seder fell asleep, thereby interrupting their meal,

chunks.en: they may eat. All of them,
chunks.st: they may eat from the Paschal lamb when they awake. If the entire company fell asleep,

chunks.en: they may not eat.
chunks.st: they may not eat any more.
chunks.stMore: If they all fall asleep, this is considered a complete interruption, and if they were to resume their meal it would be akin to eating the offering in two different places.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: if they dozed, they may eat.
chunks.st: If they dozed they may eat from the Paschal lamb when they awake,

chunks.en: If they fell fast asleep, they may not eat.
chunks.st: but if they fell fast asleep they may not eat from it.

summary: The korban Pesach after midnight makes hands tamei. This mishnah also teaches whether the bracha on the korban Pesach counts for the chagigah, and the other way around.

chunks.en: The korban Pesach after midnight
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb after midnight

chunks.en: makes the hands tamei.
chunks.explain: After midnight it may not be eaten anymore.
chunks.st: renders one’s hands ritually impure,
chunks.stMore: as it becomes notar, an offering that remained after the time when they may be eaten has expired;

chunks.en: Piggul and nosar
chunks.st: and the Sages ruled that both piggul, offerings that were invalidated due to inappropriate intent while being sacrificed,

words.note: A korban made unfit by a wrong plan.
A korban left over after its time.

chunks.en: make the hands tamei.
chunks.st: and notar render one’s hands ritually impure.

chunks.en: If he said the bracha on the korban Pesach, it covers
chunks.st: If one recited the blessing over the Paschal lamb, which is: Who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us to eat the Paschal lamb, he has also exempted

chunks.en: the one on the korban.
chunks.st: himself from reciting a blessing over the Festival offering.
chunks.stMore: The blessing for the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth of Nisan is: Who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us to eat the offering.

chunks.en: If he said the one on the korban,
chunks.st: However, if he recited the blessing over the Festival offering,

chunks.en: it does not cover the one on the korban Pesach.
chunks.st: he has not exempted himself from reciting a blessing over the Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: this one does not cover that one,
chunks.st: This blessing does not exempt one from reciting a blessing over this one,

chunks.en: and that one does not cover this one.
chunks.st: and that blessing does not exempt that one, as there is a separate blessing for each offering.
